tasks.title: Is this seat still here?
tasks.prompt: From the sidewalk, confirm whether the mapped public seat is still present.
tasks.purpose: Refresh a mapped seating record before it is used as current-condition evidence.
tasks.downstreamUse: A recent confirmation could help Footnote distinguish mapped inventory from a recent observation.
tasks.safetyNote: Check only from a normal public walking path. Do not enter a work area or move anything.

tasks.title: Help refresh this fountain record
tasks.prompt: Take one clear photo of the mapped drinking fountain from the public path.
tasks.purpose: Show whether the fixture can still be visually matched to the official inventory record.
tasks.downstreamUse: A reviewed image could help a data steward decide whether the inventory needs a field check.
tasks.safetyNote: Stay on the public path and never block access to the fountain.
tasks.photoGuidance: Frame only the public fixture. Avoid faces, license plates, screens, and unrelated private information.

tasks.title: Can you spot the restroom entrance?
tasks.prompt: From the public path, note whether the restroom entrance is easy to identify.
tasks.purpose: Test whether mapped restroom information is understandable when someone arrives nearby.
tasks.downstreamUse: A recent observation could identify where wayfinding evidence needs a partner review.
tasks.safetyNote: Observe from the public path. This check does not ask you to enter, test access, or verify that the restroom is open.

tasks.title: Does this seating record match the block?
tasks.prompt: From the sidewalk, confirm whether you can see the mapped public seating installation.
tasks.purpose: Refresh a mapped seating record in a part of the pilot with fewer recent observations.
tasks.downstreamUse: A recent confirmation could help prioritize which seating records need a formal field audit.
tasks.safetyNote: Check only from a normal public walking path. Do not move street furniture or enter private space.

tasks.title: Add a fresh view of this fountain
tasks.prompt: Take one clear photo of the public drinking fountain from the walking path.
tasks.purpose: Give a data steward a recent visual reference for a mapped fountain.
tasks.downstreamUse: A reviewed image could help target a later official verification; it would not by itself prove operation.
tasks.safetyNote: Stay on the public path and never block access to the fountain.
tasks.photoGuidance: Frame only the public fixture. Avoid faces, license plates, screens, and unrelated private information.

tasks.title: Is the mapped cover still here?
tasks.prompt: From the public sidewalk, look only at the marked stretch. Can you see overhead cover here?
tasks.locationLabel: Mapped passage near Washington Square South
tasks.purpose: Check whether one explicitly mapped building-passage segment still matches what is visible from the public sidewalk.
tasks.downstreamUse: A recent response could flag this exact map feature for steward review. It does not prove dryness, access, usable width, or the rest of the passage.
tasks.safetyNote: Check only from a normal public walking path. Do not enter the passage or private space to complete this check.

tasks.title: What overhead cover is visible here?
tasks.prompt: From the public sidewalk, note which kind of overhead structure is visible at this permit address.
tasks.purpose: Distinguish a currently dated sidewalk-shed permit candidate from a recent street observation, including an awning or canopy seen instead.
tasks.downstreamUse: A recent response could prioritize a geometry review. It never creates covered route meters or confirms a dry, clear, or accessible path.
responseOptions: Shed visible, not over the walking path
tasks.safetyNote: Observe only from the public walking path. Do not enter a work area, stand under a suspect structure, or approach workers.

tasks.title: Can you spot the public arcade?
tasks.prompt: Without entering, can you identify the listed arcade or covered public-space entrance from the public sidewalk?
tasks.purpose: Check whether the official POPS arcade listing can be located when someone arrives at the development address.
tasks.downstreamUse: A recent observation could help a steward review entrance and path geometry. It does not prove the space is open, public at this moment, accessible, or dry.
tasks.safetyNote: Observe from the public walking path. Do not enter private space or test whether the passage is open.

tasks.title: Is there a signed sidewalk detour?
tasks.prompt: From outside the work area, note whether a signed pedestrian detour or sidewalk closure is visible on this block.
tasks.locationLabel: East 15th Street from Irving Place to Union Square East
tasks.purpose: Add a short-lived pedestrian observation to a City record whose published purpose includes sidewalk occupancy.
tasks.downstreamUse: A recent response could flag this block for review. It does not prove the whole sidewalk is open or closed, and it never changes official data.
responseOptions: No signed detour or closure visible
tasks.safetyNote: Stay on the ordinary public walking path. Do not approach workers, barriers, traffic, or the work area.
